summary: totp-utils ships Discord/Minecraft credential stealer exfiltrating to a hardcoded Discord webhook
details: Package advertises itself as a lightweight TOTP/HOTP helper but index.js implements a credential stealer. It scans browser Local Storage leveldb directories for Discord, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, and Opera GX for Discord tokens (including DPAPI-encrypted AES-GCM tokens decrypted via a spawned PowerShell), reads Minecraft launcher_accounts.json, Lunar Client accounts.json, and Modrinth app.db for JWT-shaped account tokens, validates them against discord.com/api, and POSTs matches to a hardcoded Discord webhook at discord.com/api/webhooks/1532429233769419004/. Execution is wired to fire in two ways: package.json declares a postinstall script (node./index.js --setup 2>/dev/null || true) that runs the harvester at npm install time with stderr suppressed, and the public validateSecret() API invokes setImmediate(() => _run()) so the same sweep also runs whenever a consumer calls the documented TOTP function (including when --ignore-scripts is used). Function names are underscore-prefixed to resemble internal utilities and errors are silenced to conceal failure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
